items.title: Depreciation methods change reported profit, not cash
items.claim: A delivery van costs £40,000 with a 4-year useful life and £8,000 residual value. Under straight-line depreciation, what is the year-1 depreciation charge?
items.reveal_title: Straight-line: (cost minus residual) divided by life
items.reveal:
(£40,000 - £8,000) / 4 = £8,000 per year. Reducing balance would front-load the charge (e.g. 40% of £40,000 = £16,000 in year 1).

Neither method affects cash flow — the van was paid for upfront. Depreciation is an accounting allocation that matches cost to revenue across periods, governed by IAS 16. Different methods produce different reported profits in early years but the same total over the asset's life.
items.why: Profit figures are sensitive to accounting policy choices. Cash flow is not. This is one reason cash flow statements were made mandatory under IAS 7.

items.title: Decline is not the end — vinyl records came back
items.claim: Vinyl record sales collapsed from the mid-1980s as CDs took over. What has happened since the late 2000s?

options.text: Vinyl sales have risen every year from 2007 to 2023, overtaking CDs in US revenue terms in 2022 for the first time since 1987 (RIAA data)

items.reveal:
RIAA US data: vinyl revenue fell to under $20m by 2006. By 2022, vinyl revenue was $1.2bn — overtaking CDs ($483m) for the first time in 35 years. UK Official Charts data shows similar pattern from 2008 onwards.

The textbook PLC implies decline is terminal. Brand repositioning, nostalgia and physical-product premiums in a streaming world reversed that trajectory. Other examples: Polaroid film, Kodak Super 8, mechanical watches.
items.why: The four-stage product life cycle is a framework, not a law of nature. Decline can be reversed by changing what the product means to customers.

items.title: Profitable businesses fail when cash runs out
items.claim: A construction firm books £5 million revenue and £500,000 profit in 2023 but customers pay 120 days after invoicing while suppliers demand 30 days. What is the most likely outcome?

options.text: Strong cash position because of the reported profit
A cash flow gap large enough to threaten survival, despite profitability — overtrading
Profit and cash will be identical
Suppliers must accept 120-day payment by law

items.reveal:
Carillion, the UK construction giant, reported £147 million profit in 2016 and collapsed in January 2018 with £1.5 billion of debt. A large part of the gap between profit and cash came from long receivable cycles on government contracts combined with aggressive revenue recognition.

'Profit is opinion; cash is fact' is an accounting saying with an empirical basis. The UK Insolvency Service reports that 80%+ of business failures involve a cash-flow rather than profitability problem.
items.why: Reported profit can lead, lag or diverge from cash entirely. Working capital management is often what separates surviving and failing firms.
